To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the removal of the PsaE and PsaF polypeptides in Synechococcus PS I complexes biases electron transfer in favor the PsaB cofactors, and this effect is attributed to the weakening of H‐bonds from the A0A and/or A1A cofactors to the PsaB α‐helices.
removal of the PsaE‐PsaF subcomplex in PS I complexes from Synechococus sp. PCC7002 results in a bias of electron transfer to the PsaB‐branch of cofactors.

the PsaF polypeptide is required for the maintenance of the lifetime and relative amplitude of the fast and slow electron transfer kinetic phases of A1A and A1B to FX in PS I complexes from Synechococcussp.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of PsaF in the organization of the A‐k(1) helices in the PS I core antenna, and how this organization influences electron transfer from A0 to A1.
the mechanism of electron transfer from the A‐jk α‐helix to FX and the mechanism by which PsaF controls the electron transfer pathways in photosystem I.
the mechanism by which electron transfer from A0A to A0B is biased in favor of the latter in PS I complexes lacking PsaF.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
removal of PsaF biases electron transfer in favor the PsaB cofactors, and this is consistent with the hypothesis that the PsaB and PsaA polypeptides are structurally asymmetric.
the removal of the PsaE/PsaF subunits biases the electron transfer in favor the PsaB cofactors.
the removal of the PsaD and PsaE subunits and/or the PsaF polypeptide biases electron transfer in favor the PsaB‐branch of cofactors in the PS I complex.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
removal of the PsaE and PsaF polypeptides from PS I complexes results in the same changes in the kinetics of electron transfer from the A‐center, but with different magnitudes.
the removal of the PsaE‐PsaF heterodimer biases electron transfer in favor PsaB branch, but the PsaE subunit alone does not.
the PsaF polypeptide plays a role in stabilizing the A1A− state, and that the PsaE polypeptide plays an ancillary role in this process.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the PsaF polypeptide is a key player in regulating the electron transfer properties of PS I.
the removal of the PsaE and/or PsaF polypeptides biases electron transfer in favor the PsaB subunit of PS I, but the mechanism of this bias is not yet clear.
